what.text: Noopept (international name omberacetam, code GVS-111) is the ethyl ester of N-phenylacetyl-L-prolylglycine. It is a small dipeptide-like molecule, which is why it is often grouped with peptides, and it was developed in Russia.

src.label: Deigin et al., Pharmaceutics, 2022 (review of peptide drugs developed in Russia)
Australia, Poisons Standard October 2026 (Therapeutic Goods (Poisons Standard—October 2026) Instrument 2026)

what.text: A 2022 review lists it among 14 peptide products registered in Russia, as a nootropic (a drug meant to aid thinking). A 2025 study by 12 official medicines control laboratories says it is a prescription medicine in Russia for brain injury, mood disorders and cerebral vascular disease.

src.label: Deigin et al., Pharmaceutics, 2022 (review of peptide drugs developed in Russia)
Vanhee et al., J Xenobiot, 2025 (12 official medicines control laboratories, including TGA)

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and lab studies:

items.text: In rats, it raised the activity of the genes for the nerve growth factors NGF and BDNF in the hippocampus.

src.label: Ostrovskaya et al., Bull Exp Biol Med, 2008

items.text: In mice, it prevented the spatial-memory deficit caused by scopolamine.

src.label: Belnik et al., Bull Exp Biol Med, 2007

what.text: These effects come from animal studies. They have not been confirmed in people.

research.text: Human evidence: a few small Russian studies in people with mild cognitive problems after stroke, brain injury or vascular disease, mostly published in Russian. No trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov.
A PubMed search returned 106 records; most are animal or lab studies. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial for noopept or omberacetam.

research.title: Mild cognitive impairment after stroke, 2011

open (unblinded) study with a control group; the abstract does not describe randomization

research.found: The authors report better MMSE and word-association scores after 2 months in the noopept group than in controls, and describe it as safe.

research.found: The authors report more alpha and beta activity and less delta activity, which they call typical of nootropic drugs. No clinical outcome is given in the abstract.

research.text: In a 2021 study, researchers bought 10 over-the-counter "cognitive enhancement" supplements online, labelled as containing omberacetam or related drugs. Some contained up to 40.6 mg of omberacetam per serving, about four times a typical drug dose, and 75% of declared amounts were wrong.

us.text: Noopept is not FDA approved for any use. FDA has cited products containing noopept, many sold as dietary supplements, as unapproved new drugs and/or misbranded drugs. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: in 2019 FDA sent 12 warning letters and 5 online advisory letters to companies "illegally selling more than 58 products, many that are sold as dietary supplements, which are unapproved new drugs and/or misbranded drugs" with Alzheimer's claims. FDA's list of the products cited includes noopept.

world.lead: Noopept is a prescription medicine in Russia. It is not authorized in the EU or Australia, according to official medicines laboratories, and Australia lists it as prescription-only. It is not approved in the US. WADA does not name it.

after.text: Noopept (omberacetam) is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA class S0 covers substances with no current approval by any government health authority; noopept is registered in Russia. The related drug fonturacetam (4-phenylpiracetam) is named as a stimulant banned in competition (S6.A). The lists do not say how they apply to noopept.

side.text: Side-effect data are sparse. One small Russian study describes it as safe but gives no side-effect counts. Supplements tested in 2021 contained up to four times a typical dose, and often not what the label said.

items.text: one open study in 60 stroke patients described a "high level of safety"; it gives no side-effect counts.

unconfirmed: Russia's state drug register asks for a picture code before showing results, so noopept's register entry could not be opened; its status comes from a 2022 review and a 2025 laboratory study.
The Neznamov 2009 comparison with piracetam could not be opened (the publisher returned an error) and has no PubMed abstract.
No FDA statement saying in so many words that noopept is not a lawful dietary ingredient was found; FDA's 2019 action covered products with Alzheimer's claims.
UK (MHRA) was not checked. The TGA's product register was not checked.
surprises: Noopept turns up in over-the-counter supplements, but FDA has cited noopept products as unapproved new drugs, and tested supplements contained up to four times a typical drug dose.
Australia lists noopept as a prescription-only medicine, yet no product is authorized there, per official laboratories.
